--- title: "OMOP Variant Occurrence" execute: echo: false --- ::: {.cell} ::: ### Summary The **`_variant_occurrence`** table is a custom extension to the OMOP Common Data Model (CDM) that captures detailed genetic variant information identified in patients through genomic testing. This table enables precision oncology research by providing granular variant-level data including genomic coordinates, variant types, molecular consequences, and clinical interpretations. Currently, the table contains variants identified via a range of Stanford-affiliated genomic tests, sourced from the Epic Genomics Suite starting in August 2025. The following tests are included: - **Solid tumor STAMP** - `STANFORD ACTIONABLE MUTATION PANEL FOR SOLID TUMORS` - **Heme-STAMP NGS (Next Generation Sequencing)** - `HEME-STAMP NGS PANEL, BM/TISSUE/FLUID` - `HEME-STAMP NGS, BLOOD` - **Heme-STAMP MRD (Minimal Residual Disease)** - `HEME-STAMP MRD, BONE MARROW` - `HEME-STAMP MRD, BLOOD` - **POLE** - `POLE, FFPE` - **Guardant360** - `GUARDANT360` - `GUARDANT360 CDX` - `GUARDANT360 TISSUENEXT` - `GUARDANT360 RESPONSE` - **Pharmacogenomics Panel (Stanford)** - `PHARMACOGENOMICS PANEL (STANFORD)` - **JAK2 V617F PCR** - `JAK2 V617F VARIANT DETECTION BY QUANTITATIVE PCR, BLOOD` - `JAK2 V617F VARIANT DETECTION BY QUANTITATIVE PCR, BONE MARROW/FLUID` - **Invitae Germline** - `INVITAE HEREDITARY DIAGNOSTIC CANCER PANEL` - `INVITAE CARDIOLOGY PANEL` - `INVITAE PEDIATRIC, CARDIOLOGY, NEUROLOGY, AND RARE GENETIC DISEASE PANEL` - `INVITAE REFLEX/RE-REQ RESULTS` - `INVITAE NEUROLOGY PANEL` - `INVITAE CUSTOM TEST PANEL 1` - `INVITAE STAT CANCER PANEL` - `INVITAE FAMILY VARIANT TESTING PANEL` - **Empower BRCA** - `EMPOWER BRCA1 & BRCA2 AND COMPREHENSIVE (81)` - `EMPOWER BRCA1 & BRCA2 AND MULTI-CANCER, EXPANDED (53)` Each record in the **`_variant_occurrence`** table includes: - Genomic information (chromosome, position, DNA/amino acid changes) - Variant classification (type, molecular consequence) - Clinical interpretation and assessment (tier classification) - Test metadata (test name, specimen information) - Linkage to clinical context (visit, procedure, provider) As of November 2026, this table includes **5,331** patients with **46,414** genetic variants. ### Key Considerations - Only simple variants are present in the source data; fusion variants and copy number variants are not currently reported. We expect that additional variant types will be incorporated in future releases as the dataset continues to evolve. - The OMOP variant occurrence table does not currently contain Foundation One tests or certain types of variants detected by STAMP (both of which were previously present in the Philips data). ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="40%"} ### 📊 Data Volume - **Patient Count:** 5,331 - **Ordered Tests Count:** 6,693 - **Variant Count:** 46,414 ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ### 🧬 Data Components - **Unique Genes:** 924 - **Molecular Consequences:** 3 ::: #### Test Coverage Summary The table below summarizes the number of ordered tests, unique patients, and variants captured for each test family and individual assay. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Note:** Ordered tests are counted as unique `procedure_occurrence_id` values. A single patient may appear in multiple test families, so summing patients across families exceeds the overall unique-patient count reported at the top of this page.
Show breakdown by individual test name ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
## Variant Occurrence Metrics {.tabset} This section presents key metrics and visualizations of genetic variants identified in our patient population through genomic testing (STAMP, Guardant360, Invitae, and other assays listed above). The following table shows the distribution of patients with variant data across key clinical cohorts: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Note:** Tumor board patients are identified by visit records containing "tumor board" (case-insensitive). Thoracic cancer patients are identified from NeuralFrame diagnoses with primary sites including lung, bronchus, or thymus. ### Genomic Testing Timeline The following visualization shows the monthly trend of genomic test orders over time with cumulative totals. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Note:** Each unique `procedure_occurrence_id` represents a distinct genomic test order. A single test may detect multiple variants in a patient. ::: ## Variant Characteristics {.tabset} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Top Genes The following visualization shows the most frequently mutated genes in the cohort. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Note:** Percentages shown represent the proportion of patients with variants in each gene. ### Molecular Consequences ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Key Consequence Types:** - **Missense:** Amino acid change - **Nonsense:** Premature stop codon - **Frameshift:** Reading frame disruption - **Splice site:** Affects RNA splicing ### Clinical Classification Distribution of variants by phenotype-specific variant classification. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Clinical Significance:** - **Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic:** Variants with established or strong evidence for disease association and potential therapeutic implications - **Benign/Likely Benign:** Variants with no expected clinical impact - **VUS (Variant of Uncertain Significance):** Variants requiring further investigation to determine clinical relevance - **Other classifications:** May include context-dependent or conditional pathogenicity assessments ::: ## Specimen Type and Specimen Source {.tabset} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Specimen Type Distribution of variants by specimen type. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Common Specimen Types:** - **Tissue:** Solid tumor biopsies - **Blood:** Liquid biopsies, circulating tumor DNA - **Other sources:** Bone marrow, fluid samples ### Specimen Source Distribution of variants by specimen anatomic source. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: ## Allelic Frequency Distribution {.tabset} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### By Molecular Consequence Distribution of allelic frequencies across different variant molecular consequences. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](variant_occ_files/figure-html/allelic frequency-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: **Interpretation:** Each point represents a variant's allelic frequency. The diamond markers indicate the median allelic frequency for each consequence type. Allelic frequency represents the proportion of DNA reads containing the variant allele. ### By Gene Mutation landscape showing allelic frequency distribution across the most frequently mutated genes. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](variant_occ_files/figure-html/gene landscape-1.png){width=1344} ::: ::: **Interpretation:** Each point represents a variant in a specific gene. Box plots show the distribution (median, quartiles, and range) of allelic frequencies for the top 15 most frequently mutated genes. Red diamond markers highlight the median allelic frequency per gene. Genes are ordered by median allelic frequency. ::: ## Variant Metrics by Cohort ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Thoracic Cancer {#thoracic-tumor-board-patient} This section focuses on the patients with both thoracic cancer diagnoses and tumor board presentations who have genomic variant data. These patients represent a high-complexity cohort requiring multidisciplinary care. ::: {.cell} ::: #### Gene Mutations Top genes mutated in thoracic tumor board patients. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Note:** Percentages represent the proportion of the 45 thoracic tumor board patients with variants in each gene. #### Clinical Significance Distribution of variant clinical significance in this cohort. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### Specimen Types Types of specimens collected from thoracic tumor board patients. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Pediatric Brain Tumor {#pediatric-brain-tumor} **34 of 2,792 patients** in the [pediatric brain tumor cohort](brain_tumor_cohort.qmd) have a named genomic test in their variant records. Each patient counts once in this summary, even if they had several test types. The chart shows up to 20 named assays by unique patient count. Percentages use the full cohort. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Top genes by unique patient count (up to 20):** BRAF, CREBBP, CTNNB1, H3-3A, SMARCB1, BRCA2, DICER1, IGF1R, NF2, TACC3, TP53, TSC2, APC, AR, ARID1A, ATRX, BAP1, BCOR, BCR, CCND2. ::: These results are subject to the access and reporting controls required for PHI-containing data. ### Source Code The source code for this page can be found [here](https://github.com/susom/starr-oncology-data-lake-arpah/tree/main/src/nov_2026/variant_occ.qmd), and the SQL queries that support these metrics can be found [here](https://github.com/susom/starr-oncology-data-lake-arpah/tree/main/src/sql_std_phi/omop/variant_occ/feb26).
